bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the pharmacist salary under the Pharmacy Industry Award

If you are a pharmacist or an employer in the pharmacy sector, knowing the correct minimum pay rates is essential. The **pharmacist salary** is governed by the Pharmacy Industry Award 2020 [MA000012], which sets minimum hourly and weekly rates for pharmacists, pharmacy assistants, and interns. This article explains how the award compares to the National Minimum Wage, how to calculate annual pay, and what additional payments such as casual loading and superannuation apply.

### Award rates vs National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, or $1,004.90 per week. However, the Pharmacy Industry Award provides much higher minimum rates. For example, a full-time pharmacist (level 1) must be paid at least $41.74 per hour, or $1,586.30 per week. This is over 50% above the national minimum. The award also classifies experienced pharmacists, pharmacists in charge, and pharmacist managers at higher rates, up to $52.15 per hour for a pharmacist manager.

### How to calculate annual pharmacist salary

To estimate your annual gross pay, use the formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For a full-time pharmacist working 38 ordinary hours per week at $41.74 per hour, the annual salary is approximately $41.74 × 38 × 52 = $82,478.24. This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. You can use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to quickly convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, or weekly figures.

### Fortnightly and weekly pay

Award employees are typically paid weekly or fortnightly. For a pharmacist earning $1,586.30 per week, the fortnightly pay would be $3,172.60. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides include these weekly rates for each classification. Remember that penalty rates apply for work outside ordinary hours, such as evenings, Saturdays, and Sundays, which can increase your take-home pay.

### Casual loading for pharmacists

Casual employees under the award receive a 25% loading on the minimum hourly rate for ordinary hours. For a pharmacist, the casual rate is $52.18 per hour ($41.74 × 1.25). This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave entitlements. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to apply it correctly. Note that casual loading is not paid on overtime hours.

### Superannuation paid on top

Employers must contribute superannuation guarantee at 12% of ordinary earnings on top of the pharmacist’s base salary. For a full-time pharmacist earning $1,586.30 per week, the super contribution is an additional $190.36 per week. The super guarantee is subject to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). This means super is paid in addition to the salary, not deducted from it. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more details.

### Tax on pharmacist salary

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates, a pharmacist earning $82,478 annually would pay tax as follows: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on the next $26,800 ($4,020), 30% on the remaining $37,478 ($11,243.40), plus a 2% Medicare levy. The estimated tax would be around $15,263 plus Medicare. This is an estimate only; individual circumstances vary. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator can help you estimate your net income.

### Other award provisions

The Pharmacy Industry Award also includes allowances such as district allowance, laundry allowance, and motor vehicle allowance. Penalty rates apply for early morning, evening, and weekend work. For example, a pharmacist working Saturday morning (7 am to 8 am) receives $83.48 per hour. These extras can significantly boost your actual earnings beyond the base pharmacist salary.

### Conclusion

Whether you are negotiating a salary or checking your pay, understanding the difference between the National Minimum Wage and the award rate is crucial. The pharmacist salary under the Pharmacy Industry Award is well above the minimum, with additional loadings and penalties for casual and non-standard hours. Use our [reference tables](/data) to see full classification rates, and always refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman for the most current award information.
